title: Coaching a Robotic Sonographer: Learning Robotic Ultrasound with Sparse Expert’s Feedback
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem of improving training efficiency and performance in robotic ultrasound (RUS) systems by incorporating sparse real-time expert coaching. The authors argue that while prior work in RUS has focused on learning from demonstrations or self-supervised reinforcement learning, it has not examined active expert engagement during training.

The proposed approach combines soft actor-critic reinforcement learning with sparse corrective feedback from expert sonographers. Coaching is formalized as a partially observable Markov decision process, where expert corrections are used to update both the policy and reward structure. The expert feedback is delivered as kinesthetic corrections to the robot arm during training, and the corrected trajectories are used to refine the policy through replay-buffer updates and KL-regularized policy learning.

The empirical evaluation uses a robotic ultrasound setup with a Sawyer 7-DOF arm, a Telemed probe, and urinary bladder phantoms. Human expert sonographers provided sparse coaching while the robot learned to acquire high-quality ultrasound images. The study reports that coaching improved convergence speed and increased the number of high-quality images acquired, suggesting that real-time expert feedback can substantially improve robotic ultrasound learning.

identified_tools.name: ITS (General)
identified_tools.description: A general intelligent tutoring or coaching system that adapts guidance based on learner actions and feedback.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper proposes and tests a coaching framework for robotic ultrasound training using sparse expert corrective feedback during reinforcement learning, which functions as a general coaching/tutoring system rather than a named product.

findings.finding_summary: In phantom testing, adding coaching improved learning efficiency. Policies coached every 20k and 10k timesteps converged at approximately 150k and 120k steps, respectively, versus no convergence by 200k steps for the no-coaching condition; coaching every 5k steps converged at 100k steps. The authors report an approximate 25% improvement in convergence rate.
findings.measure: Training convergence rate / number of training steps to convergence

findings.finding_summary: Coaching improved task performance on urinary bladder phantoms P0 and P1. For P0, the number of high-quality images (HQI) increased from 2.1 �b1 0.5 without coaching to 8.2 �b1 4.6 with coaching every 20k steps, and further to 21.5 �b1 2.3 with coaching every 5k steps. For P1, HQI increased from 1.5 �b1 0.3 without coaching to 5.9 �b1 1.6 with coaching every 20k steps, and to 16.2 �b1 2.9 with coaching every 5k steps; the abstract reports a 74.4% increase in HQI on phantom testing.
findings.measure: Number of high-quality ultrasound images (q  4) during execution trials on phantoms P0 and P1

quality_tier_rationale: This is a robotics/controls framework paper, not an education study, and it does not evaluate a K-12 instructional AI tool or coaching product in classrooms. The evidence is experimental but entirely outside the target domain, so it is not usable as educational AI efficacy evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported gains are specific to robotic ultrasound training and do not translate to K-12 teaching or lesson-plan feedback. No educational impact on teachers, students, or schools is measured.
